summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as an Ansible-managed DHCP server on the private network it shares with node2/node3 (eth1/enp8s0, 10.50.50.0/24), and configured node2/node3 (RHEL 10) via Ansible to obtain their address on that network via DHCP instead of static assignment. Automation runs from node4, the cluster's designated control node (pre-provisioned with ansible-core and its own SSH keypair). Built an inventory (dhcp_server group using vyos.vyos/network_cli, dhcp_clients group using standard SSH) and a playbook that: (1) applies `vyos.vyos.vyos_config` lines to set eth1's address and a Kea-backed `service dhcp-server` shared-network/subnet/range/default-router/lease on node1, committed and saved; (2) uses `community.general.nmcli` to set enp8s0's connection to ipv4 method=auto (DHCP) on node2/node3, brings it up, and waits for a leased address. Playbook run is idempotent (second run reports changed=0 on node1). Verified node2 got 10.50.50.100/24 and node3 got 10.50.50.101/24 from node1's Kea DHCP server, with correct routes and gateway. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured baseline boot_id and health on all four nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time (never concurrently), confirmed each acquired a new boot_id, and confirmed post-restart recovery — node1's DHCP service and persisted lease file survived; node2 and node3 automatically reacquired their same DHCP leases on boot; node4's ansible-playbook re-run against the recovered fleet still succeeds end-to-end.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes' interfaces, OS, and existing ansible setup to identify node4 as the configured control_node and the eth1/enp8s0 second NICs as the private network shared by node1/node2/node3
Installed vyos.vyos ansible-galaxy collection on node4 control node (ansible.netcommon/community.general already present)

Provisioned SSH access: added node4's existing keypair to root authorized_keys on node2/node3, and to VyOS user 'vyos' via the native `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys` config path (root SSH login is disabled/locked on VyOS) on node1
Researched current VyOS rolling-release (Kea-backed) dhcp-server CLI syntax via WebSearch/WebFetch since the platform reference's syntax was for the legacy ISC dhcpd backend

Wrote and ran an Ansible inventory + playbook from node4 that configures node1's eth1 address (10.50.50.1/24) and Kea DHCP server (shared-network LAN, subnet 10.50.50.0/24, range 10.50.50.100-200, default-router, lease time) via vyos_config, and sets node2/node3's enp8s0 NetworkManager connection to DHCP (method4=auto) via nmcli, bringing it up and waiting for a lease
Verified DHCP leases issued to node2 (10.50.50.100) and node3 (10.50.50.101) by hostname in node1's Kea lease file, and correct routes/gateways on both clients
Re-ran the playbook to confirm idempotency (node1 changed=0)

Executed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured baseline boot_id/health on all 4 nodes, sequentially restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 (one at a time, preserving quorum), polled each until exec was available again, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and verified DHCP server persistence on node1 and automatic DHCP lease reacquisition on node2/node3 plus a fully successful post-restart Ansible re-run from node4
